name: Temple Watch (Mishmar HaMikdash)
notes: Laws and procedures of the priestly and Levitical guard watch in the Temple, including the officer of the Temple Mount, beating of sleeping watchmen, and burning of clothes

name: Temple Gates (Sha'arei HaMikdash)
notes: The specific gates of the Temple Mount and Temple Courtyard, their names, purposes, and special features including the gates of Nicanor, Huldah, Kiponus, Taddi, and others

name: Beit HaMoked (Fire Chamber)
notes: The fire chamber in the Temple where priests slept and kept watch, its structure, chambers, and the key-storage arrangements

name: Temple Mount Dimensions and Layout
notes: The precise measurements and layout of the Temple Mount (500x500 cubits), its sections, and the Soreg partition

name: Soreg (Temple Mount Lattice Fence)
notes: The ten-handbreadth lattice fence separating the outer Temple Mount from the Hel, including the thirteen breaches made by the Greek kings and the thirteen prostrations instituted after repair

name: Hel (Temple Rampart)
notes: The ten-cubit wide rampart between the Soreg and the courtyard steps

name: Altar Dimensions and Structure
notes: Precise measurements and construction of the outer altar, including the foundation, surround, horns, and ramp; the red dividing line between upper and lower blood applications

name: Kevesh (Altar Ramp)
notes: The ramp leading up to the altar, its dimensions (32 cubits long, 16 wide), location on the south side, and the window for disqualified bird offerings

name: Altar Stones — Prohibition of Iron
notes: Requirement that altar stones be whole (unhewn), the disqualification by iron touch, and the whitewashing schedule of the altar

name: Ezrat Nashim (Women's Courtyard)
notes: The Women's Courtyard in the Temple: its dimensions (135x135 cubits), four corner chambers (Nazirites, wood, those with skin disease, oil), and the balcony added for separation of men and women

name: Ezrat Yisrael (Israelites' Courtyard)
notes: The Court of Israel, its dimensions (135x11 cubits), and its separation from the Court of the Priests by a row of mosaic stones

name: Ezrat Kohanim (Priests' Courtyard)
notes: The Court of the Priests, its dimensions, its height relative to the Court of Israel, and the thirteen prostrations made there

name: Ulam (Temple Porch)
notes: The entrance porch of the Temple Sanctuary: its dimensions (40 cubits high, 20 cubits wide), the five ash beams over the doorway, cedar poles, golden chains, and the golden vine

name: Golden Vine of the Temple (Gefen shel Zahav)
notes: The golden vine at the door of the Sanctuary upon which worshippers would hang donated leaves, grapes, and bunches

name: Ta'im (Temple Cells/Side Chambers)
notes: The thirty-eight cells surrounding the Hekhal on three sides, their arrangement in three stories, widths, and interconnecting doors

name: Mesibah (Temple Winding Stairway/Walkway)
notes: The winding walkway used to ascend to the roofs of the cells and upper chamber, going from the northeast corner around the north and west sides

name: Upper Chamber (Aliyah) of the Temple
notes: The upper chamber above the Hekhal, its dimensions, the trap doors for workmen to descend in baskets for repairs without gazing at the Holy of Holies

name: Lishkat HaGazit (Chamber of Hewn Stone)
notes: The chamber of hewn stone in the Temple courtyard where the Great Sanhedrin sat to judge priestly fitness; the procedures for disqualified and qualified priests

name: Lishkat HaMelach (Salt Chamber)
notes: The chamber in the Temple courtyard where salt for the offerings was stored

name: Lishkat HaParvah (Parvah Chamber)
notes: The chamber in the Temple courtyard where animal hides were salted; the High Priest's mikveh was on its roof for use on Yom Kippur

name: Fifteen Steps (of the Temple)
notes: The fifteen semi-circular steps leading from the Court of Women to the Court of Israel, corresponding to the fifteen Songs of Ascent in Psalms, upon which the Levites sang

name: Temple Procession — Entering and Exiting Right
notes: The custom of entering the Temple Mount by the right and circling to the right, and the exceptions for mourners and the excommunicated with their respective exchanges of comfort

name: Gate of Nicanor (Sha'ar Nicanor)
notes: The eastern gate of the Temple courtyard, the miracle associated with it (or its gleaming copper), and why it was not replaced with gold like the other gates

name: Hekhal Dimensions
notes: Detailed measurements of the Hekhal (100x100x100 cubits), its walls, porch, Holy of Holies, side cells, and the full east-west and north-south calculations

name: Spikes on Temple Roof (Zahavit/Kelayot Orev)
notes: The iron spikes placed on the roof of the Temple to prevent birds from perching and soiling it; dispute whether included in height measurement
